events.title: Construction of the Berlin Wall Begins
events.description: East German authorities closed the border between East and West Berlin overnight, first with barbed wire and then with concrete blocks, to stop mass emigration to the West.
events.significance: The Berlin Wall became the most potent physical symbol of the Cold War and the division of Europe, remaining in place until its fall in November 1989.

events.title: Fall of Tenochtitlan
events.description: After a siege of nearly three months, Spanish conquistador Hernán Cortés and his indigenous allies captured the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan and its last emperor, Cuauhtémoc.
events.significance: The fall marked the end of the Aztec Empire and the beginning of Spanish colonial rule in Mexico, reshaping the Americas.

events.title: Birth of Lucy Stone
events.description: Lucy Stone, an American abolitionist and suffragist, was born in Massachusetts. She became the first woman from Massachusetts to earn a college degree and kept her own surname after marriage.
events.significance: Stone was a leading figure in the women's rights and anti-slavery movements and helped found the American Woman Suffrage Association.

events.title: Birth of Fidel Castro
events.description: Fidel Castro was born in Birán, Cuba. He later led the Cuban Revolution that overthrew Fulgencio Batista in 1959 and governed Cuba for nearly five decades.
events.significance: Castro established the first communist state in the Western Hemisphere and was a central figure in Cold War events such as the Cuban Missile Crisis.

events.title: Invention of the Coin-Operated Telephone Patented
events.description: William Gray received a patent for the first coin-operated public telephone, which was installed in Hartford, Connecticut.
events.significance: The pay telephone made telephone service widely accessible to the public and became a fixture of communication for over a century.
